newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel cabinet sends land plan to committee.
newsitem.headline: Israel cabinet sends land plan to committee.

text.p: The Israeli cabinet sent a proposal for creating an inventory of land for development to a committee for study but left the remaining agenda of structural reforms unfinished, a Treasury spokesman said on Wednesday.

The meeting was the second held by the cabinet to approve a package of 25 measures for structural reforms aimed at enhancing competitiveness in the economy and making the public sector more efficient.
The previous meeting, on January 8, adjourned after ministers approved 17 of the measures.
Today's meeting lasted two hours, sources said, as Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon objected to the terms of the Treasury's land plan.

The Treasury is seeking to create an inventory of state-owned land zoned for 400,000 housing units by the year 1999. The proposal is to complete all the administrative requirements needed for the land to speed development after it is tendered by the Israel Lands Administration to developers.
The Treasury plan called for 75 percent of the land to be in the centre of the country, where demand for housing is the strongest.

Sharon, however, sought to head a committee that would decide how to parcel out the land, with the aim of apportioning more to outlying areas with the aim of dispersing Israel's population, the sources said.
A committee headed by Avigdor Lieberman, director-general of the prime minister's office, will study the matter and report back within 30 days, the cabinet decided.
